title: Production Tetris
prompt: Build a production-quality Tetris game that runs locally. Treat this as a small full-stack product: a polished browser frontend, a deterministic game-engine/data layer, and a local backend API for persistence and review artifacts. Do not use paid services. Prefer simple dependencies. The app must be easy for a reviewer to run, inspect, test, and score.

frontend: Responsive browser UI that works on desktop, tablet, and phone widths.
Polished board, ghost piece, hold panel, next queue, score/level/lines, pause/game-over overlays, and clear visual feedback for lock, line clear, hold, level up, and invalid actions.
Keyboard controls for move, rotate clockwise/counterclockwise, soft drop, hard drop, hold, pause/resume, restart, and mute/settings.
Touch/on-screen controls that are usable on phone-sized screens without page scroll fighting the game.
Accessible labels or help text for controls and status, readable contrast, and no layout clipping at common viewport sizes.
backend: A local Node HTTP backend or equivalent local API layer serving the app and JSON endpoints.
Versioned local persistence for high scores, settings, saved game summaries, and replay metadata without external services.
Endpoints or documented local APIs for health, high-score list/update, replay save/list, and settings load/save.
Input validation for persisted records and safe handling of corrupt/invalid stored data.
Deterministic seven-bag randomizer with seed support so a replay can be reproduced from seed plus input log.
gameplay: All seven tetrominoes spawn, rotate with wall kicks, collide, lock, clear lines, and top out correctly.
Fair seven-bag randomizer, hold piece, ghost piece, next-piece queue of at least five pieces, soft drop, hard drop, lock delay, scoring, level progression, and pause/restart/game-over states.
Game loop remains stable under fast repeated input and after pause/resume/restart cycles.
verification: Automated tests or scripted checks for game engine logic, seven-bag fairness, scoring/line clears, hold/queue behavior, replay determinism, and backend persistence validation.
README with setup, run, test, and preview instructions.
Final benchmark report with checks run, limitations, token/session evidence if available, and artifact refs.

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend meets responsive, polished, accessible Tetris UI requirements.
Backend/local API persists validated high scores, settings, saved game summaries, and replay metadata.
All core Tetris gameplay rules work: pieces, rotation/wall kicks, collision, locking, line clears, hold, ghost, queue, scoring, levels, pause, restart, and game over.
Seeded seven-bag randomizer and replay metadata allow deterministic reproduction of at least one saved game path.
Keyboard and touch controls are both complete and usable.
Automated/scripted checks cover frontend-adjacent logic, backend persistence/API behavior, and game engine correctness.
Reviewer can run locally, view the app, run tests, and inspect artifacts without paid services.
requiredArtifacts: preview URL or local run command
Pi session ref and CodeWiki trace refs when applicable
